en: The Upasena Sūtra.
Wal_2_1 Siddham. The setting was Rājagṛha.
Wal_2_2 At that time, the Venerable Upasena was staying at Rājagṛha in the Śītavana cemetery, on the slope of the Sarpaśauṇḍika mountain, in the Kaliṅga-pavilions.

Then, while the venerable Upasena was alone, in seclusion, and in meditative retreat, a venomous snake of fierce majesty and terrible poison—small as a collyrium-stick—fell upon his body. Thereupon, the venerable Upasena addressed the monks: "A venomous snake, small as a collyrium-stick, has fallen upon my body.
Venerable sirs, please take hold of my body from all sides and carry it outside; let it not die right here."
"It will fall apart just like a handful of chaff.
At that time, the venerable Śāriputra was sitting not far from the venerable Upasena, leaning against the foot of a certain tree.
The venerable Śāriputra heard the speech uttered by the venerable Upasena, and having heard it, he approached the venerable Upasena. Having approached, [he addressed] the venerable Upasena...
He said this:
"Indeed, we do not perceive any alteration in the face or any change in the faculties of the venerable Upasena; yet the venerable Upasena says: 'A venomous snake has fallen upon my body.'"

As before, up to: "It is just like a handful of chaff. Venerable Śāriputra, whoever should think thus: "I am the eye; the eye is mine. I am the ear, nose, tongue, body; I am the mind; the mind is mine. I am form; form is mine. I am sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena..."

"The dharmas are mine; the earth element is mine, the earth element belongs to me; I am the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, and the consciousness element; the form aggregate is I, the form aggregate belongs to me; I am the feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness aggregates;
the consciousness aggregate belongs to me. For such a person, there would be a change in the face or a transformation in the sense faculties.

But it does not occur to me thus: "I am the eye, the eye is mine," or "I am the aggregate of consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness is mine. [If that were so,] what would there be for me—either a change in the face or a transformation of the faculties?
Indeed, for a long time, Venerable Upasena, the underlying tendencies of the conceit "I am," the notion "mine," and the deep-seated attachment to the pride "I am" have been present.
"They have been abandoned and fully understood; their roots are cut off like the head of a palm tree, rendered incapable of further becoming, and subject to the law of non-arising in the future.
What change will there be in his face, or what alteration in his faculties?
Then the Venerable Śāriputra, having taken hold of the body of the Venerable Upasena from all sides, carried it outside.
Immediately after [this was] accomplished, the body of the venerable Upasena shattered into a hundred pieces, just like a handful of chaff.
Then, at that time, the venerable Śāriputra spoke these verses:
“When this holy life has been well-practiced and this path has been well-cultivated,”
One becomes joyful at the exhaustion of life, like one who has discarded a vessel of poison.
When this holy life has been well-practiced and this path well-cultivated,
one is satisfied at the end of life, just as one is upon the departure of a disease.
When this holy life has been well-practiced and this path well-cultivated,
one is freed like escaping from a burning house and does not grieve at the end of life.
When, through well-practiced holy life and this path well-cultivated,
one perceives with wisdom the world as being like dry wood, [one is liberated].

Then the Venerable Śāriputra, having performed the funeral honors for the body of the Venerable Upasena, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows.

Venerable sir, a venomous snake of fierce brilliance and terrible poison, as small as a finger-stick, fell upon the body of the venerable Bhadanta Upasena; [the rest] is as before, until his body was shattered like a handful of chaff.
Śāriputra, had these verses and these mantra-words been recited to the noble son Upasena at that time, the venomous snake would not have overcome his body.
His body will not disintegrate like a handful of chaff.
"Venerable sir, what are those verses? What are those mantra-words?"
I have loving-kindness for the Dhṛtarāṣṭras and for the Airāvaṇas;
I have loving-kindness for the Chibbāputras and for the Kamvala- and Aśvatara-nāgas.
I have loving-kindness for the Karkoṭakas and the Kṛṣṇagautamas;
and I always have loving-kindness for those nāgas who are Nanda and Upananda.
I have loving-kindness for those without feet, and I have loving-kindness for those with two feet;
I have loving-kindness for those with four feet, and I have loving-kindness for those with many feet.
I have loving-kindness for all nāgas— those nāgas who dwell in the ocean—
and I have loving-kindness for all sentient beings, whether they be weak or stable.
May all sentient beings indeed be happy; may all sentient beings be free from illness;
may they all behold auspicious things, and may no evil come upon them.
While I was constantly dwelling on the Sarpaśauṇḍika Slope,
a serpent of terrible venom threatened my life.
By that word of truth through which my Teacher is unsurpassed in the worlds,
by that word of truth may no poison take effect upon my body.
Lust, hatred, and delusion—these are the three poisons in the world.
The Blessed Buddha is free from poison; the True Dharma has destroyed the poison.
The poison is destroyed, the terrible poison is destroyed; the protective rite has been performed.
All those pierced by poison have had their poison destroyed; O serpent, the poison is destroyed!

In this regard, these mantra-words are as follows: *otuṃbile*, *tuṃbile*, *tuṃbe*, *pratuṃbe*, *naṭṭe*, *sunaṭṭe*, *kevaṭṭe*, *munaye*, *samaye*, *datte*, *nīlakeśe*, *vālakupe*, *ole*, *oṅko*, *svāhā*.
"Śāriputra, if at that time these verses and these mantra-words had occurred to the mind of the young man Upasena, the venomous snake would not have entered his body,

nor would his body have perished like a handful of chaff. Reverend sir, how could it be possible for the Venerable Upasena, at that moment, to have spoken verses never heard before, or mantra-words never heard before?"
Just as it is now with the Blessed One.
Then the Venerable Śāriputra, having rejoiced and delighted in the words spoken by the Blessed One, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and departed from the Blessed One's presence.
